scope: Real terminal-dialogue transport through the embedded MCP App in a regular ChatGPT chat, using the opt-in live spec's isolated browser context with a clearly labelled synthetic question, synthetic curriculum and progress text. No real save, learner progress, private conversation or curriculum packet was sent or changed. No OpenAI API key or paid model call was used.
host: Regular ChatGPT web client (chatgpt.com) in the user's signed-in Chrome, existing zombie-escape-study-game custom MCP plugin with OAuth; tools refreshed from Settings → Plugins → zombie-escape-study-game → Manage → Refresh tools after the relay restart; fresh chat started from the plugin page.
relay: npm run bridge:stop then bridge:start with the new relay tools; tunnel started through the local start-public control and verified; live study requests released through the local enable control only for the test and disabled again afterwards. Queue was idle (0 queued, 0 working) before release.

steps.action: Asked the fresh chat to call open_study_terminal (not the demo, no get_study_handoff, no polling).
steps.observed: ChatGPT called open_study_terminal once. The live app rendered in the side panel with 'Waiting for your game terminal', '0 turns answered' and 'Connected. Waiting for a terminal message from your game…'. The chat reported Mode: Live game, Polling: Disabled. Relay status showed terminalRelay.sessions 1, workerActive false.

steps.action: The live spec sent 'I think [2,3] is the largest window.' from the isolated game terminal (mode terminal-dialogue, synthetic question).
steps.observed: The app claimed the queued job, posted its @study prompt through ui/message, and a model turn started with no chat typing. ChatGPT called reply_study_terminal_job with complete:false; the panel showed the learner message, the Terminal AI follow-up and '1 turn answered'; the game rendered the tutor reply with keys 0 and the request applied.

steps.action: The spec sent the complete explanation from the game terminal.
steps.observed: The app posted a second @study turn. ChatGPT called reply_study_terminal_job with complete:true ('Exercise completed' in the chat). The panel showed '2 turns answered' and returned to waiting. The game applied the existing once-only reward: keys 1, encounter consumed, both tutor requests applied, and the learner ledger unchanged by the development profile.

relayDiagnostics.note: tools/call includes the app's bounded claim and read refreshes. No legacy worker session existed; get_study_handoff was never called. Sharing was disabled again after the run.
relayDiagnostics.redaction: Counts only; the relay never retains bodies, headers, credentials or OAuth identifiers.

limitations: Only the synthetic live-spec question was exercised; the synthetic curriculum and progress text are short, so the size-bounded prompt included them inline and read_study_terminal_context was never called live.

The @study prompt posted through ui/message is not shown as a user bubble; the model's reply text appeared as part of the assistant's response. Only the reply_study_terminal_job text reaches the game.
Composer text beginning with @study was converted by ChatGPT into its Study mode chip in the first message; this does not establish native Study Mode for the relayed turns.
This proves the host-turn transport and once-only reward for one chat and one OAuth owner. Real model grading quality is not certified by it.
